rule: GOAL: Arrange four colored tiles to match the sequence shown in the top row. CONTROLS: Click a tile in the bottom palette to select it, then click a slot in the center box to place it. RULE: The center box slots correspond directly to the left-to-right order of the target colors above. TRAP: Thinking you must click slots first; you must always select a palette tile before placing it.

GOAL: Navigate the blue block to the goal by sliding across the grid. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the block; it continues sliding until it hits a wall or solid floor. RULE: Gray tiles are ice; you slide over them and only stop on white tiles or walls. TRAP: Believing gray tiles stop movement wastes turns; they are slippery, not solid.

GOAL: Align the yellow plug with the yellow gap. CONTROLS: Top blue shifts boundaries left; bottom blue shifts them right. RULE: The gray area acts as a linked seesaw, maintaining a constant total width. TRAP: Believing the boundaries move independently wastes time; they always change in opposite directions.

GOAL: Move the token to the target by clicking nearby items. CONTROLS: Click adjacent dots to swap places; click distant crosses to jump directly to them. RULE: Dots only swap if immediately next to the token; crosses allow longer jumps. TRAP: Assuming clicks work at any distance wasted time probing far points that did nothing.

GOAL: Align the sliding plug with the gap on the far right side. CONTROLS: Click blue buttons to shift gray segments left or right. RULE: Moving one segment pushes the adjacent segment in the opposite direction. TRAP: Clicking repeatedly until a button stops working locks the adjacent segment at the edge.

GOAL: Fill two cups by directing liquid streams into their cavities. CONTROLS: Space pours liquid; arrows move the bar. RULE: Liquid must enter cups without touching walls or floor. TRAP: Assuming liquid stays contained; it spreads on surfaces, requiring precise alignment to avoid contamination.

GOAL: Guide the plug into the cup by programming its path with five directional steps. CONTROLS: Click horizontal or vertical bars to set each mark’s direction; click the ball to run the sequence. RULE: Setting both bars on a mark makes the plug move down; the plug must travel five cells down to reach the cup. TRAP: Assuming the animation’s return to home means failure; the level actually completes at the animation’s end if the path was correct.

GOAL: Match the flashing frame's color to the empty slot's color, then fill it using the palette. CONTROLS: Click the frame to read its color, click the matching palette tile, then click the slot. Press SPACE to confirm the move. RULE: Only the red-and-white flashing components indicate the current target pair. TRAP: Do not click the pre-placed green tile; it is static and not a target.

GOAL: Align each column's glyph to match its specific shape partner from the bank. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the cursor between columns and cycle glyphs within a column. RULE: A glyph is correct if its shape matches the target, regardless of rotation or flip. TRAP: Assuming UP always advances the cycle forward; DOWN often reaches the target faster by cycling backward.

GOAL: Place all colored tiles into their matching colored slots. CONTROLS: Left-click to pick up a tile, left-click again to drop it, and press Space to cycle through tile colors or states. RULE: A tile only fits into a slot that shares its exact color and shape. TRAP: Assuming a tile is solid when it is hollow; checking the border color reveals the true identity.

GOAL: Align three floating platforms to specific heights to match target rows. CONTROLS: Click buttons between platforms to raise the left neighbor and lower the right one. RULE: Each click transfers one unit of height from the right platform to the left. TRAP: Assuming buttons raise the right side; they actually lower it while raising the left.

ESTABLISHED: Pushing right shifts the entire attached chain one cell, moving the driver block to the rod's new tip position. Attached blocks always sit immediately left of the rod. FAILED: Assuming the driver stays behind the rod or that only the tip moves without dragging the whole chain. GOAL IS NOT: Just extending the rod to a specific length; blocks must be physically relocated via chain pushes. CONTROLS: Right extends the rod, pulling attached blocks into the new tip slot. Left retracts, leaving blocks behind. Up/Down moves the rod vertically, dragging attached blocks along.

ESTABLISHED: SPACE attaches or detaches an adjacent box. Attached boxes maintain a fixed world-space offset relative to the player, not rotating with the player's facing direction. The target tube is located at rows 28-31, columns 28-39. FAILED: Pressing SPACE to detach while the box was visually positioned inside the tube rightmost cell did not complete the level. GOAL IS NOT: Simply moving the attached box into the tube's visual area. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player. SPACE toggles box attachment if facing it. Attached boxes follow without rotating.

GOAL: Place the white box into the blue tube. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player; Space attaches or detaches a box. RULE: Attached boxes move with the player but do not rotate their orientation. TRAP: Thinking the box rotates with the player; it stays fixed in world space relative to the offset.

GOAL: Place tiles to form the target pattern. CONTROLS: Click tiles to move them. Press space to confirm the move. RULE: Space must register a change; if it reports no effect, the next action fails. TRAP: Assuming space is always a safe filler. A no-op space poisons the queue, causing the following click to error.

ESTABLISHED: The key tip alternates between 4x4 and 2x2 states upon syncing. The lock pins are purple, while the keypad lights up white or green. FAILED: Entering the cross code with an expanded tip did not clear the level. Pressing cells on a gray base without white lights failed to trigger events. GOAL IS NOT: Simply matching the tip's color to the handle or locking the tip in a specific corner position. CONTROLS: Clicking the lock center syncs the key. Pressing keypad cells changes their state to green, potentially triggering a color flash.

GOAL: Align two shape tokens so their corners touch diagonally, allowing them to merge into a larger form. CONTROLS: Clicking a grid cell instantly moves the selected token’s pivot to that location, regardless of distance. RULE: Tokens only merge when positioned diagonally adjacent; overlapping cells or direct side contact causes a collision instead. TRAP: Thinking movement requires a clear path; tokens teleport to the clicked pivot, ignoring intermediate obstacles entirely.

GOAL: Slide the player to a safe spot below the enemy without being caught in its two-cell lunge. CONTROLS: Arrow keys slide the player until hitting a wall or white tile. RULE: The enemy lunges two cells toward the player if they are within three cells horizontally. TRAP: Thinking the enemy only attacks the landing cell; it actually kills anything in its path, so standing directly in front is fatal.

GOAL: Eliminate three enemies by moving into their cells. CONTROLS: Arrows move one step; entering an enemy cell destroys it. RULE: Enemies lunge only within their facing line if unobstructed. TRAP: Assuming distant cells were safe when a closer enemy actually blocked the line of sight.

GOAL: Align both crosses so their arms cover the scattered target dots. CONTROLS: Arrows shift the active cross three cells; Space switches between the yellow and blue crosses. RULE: Each cross has fixed arm lengths, so the center must land exactly where the dot-pair lines intersect. TRAP: Believing arrows moved the cross by one cell led to wasted moves; each press actually shifts it three.

GOAL: Match each colored key to its matching cross by extending the tip into the center. CONTROLS: Clicking a lock panel grows the key; the panel farther from the start extends it, the closer one shrinks it. RULE: Keys only fit crosses of the same color, and the tip must land exactly on the red center dot. TRAP: Assuming any panel works; clicking the wrong side retracts the key, wasting moves and potentially missing the target.

GOAL: Rotate the ring so the left and right sides match each other. CONTROLS: Left arrow rotates the ring counter-clockwise; right arrow rotates it clockwise. RULE: The two arrows at the middle point outward, indicating the specific tiles that must align horizontally. TRAP: Assuming the arrows shifted only one row; they actually rotate the entire ring, keeping the top and bottom rows fixed relative to each other.

GOAL: Align three shapes to cover all colored dots. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selected shape; Space cycles to the next shape. RULE: Dots are cleared only when their exact pixel lies on a shape's line. TRAP: Assuming visual overlap suffices; precise geometric alignment with dot centers is required.

GOAL: Reduce the board to a single remaining piece. CONTROLS: Click a piece to select it, then click a highlighted spot to jump. RULE: You can only jump over an adjacent piece into an empty space. TRAP: Assuming any piece can move; pieces with no adjacent neighbors are stuck.

GOAL: Match the bottom-right grid to its specific hub pattern. CONTROLS: Clicking a hub cell inverts the corresponding panel cell’s color. RULE: Three hubs show inverse patterns, but the bottom-right hub displays the exact target colors. TRAP: Assuming every hub acts as a simple inverse key wasted time on the bottom-right panel.

GOAL: Guide the white handle to place the bead on the purple square. CONTROLS: Move the white cross; the gray cross stays fixed; the bead follows the midpoint. RULE: The bead always sits exactly halfway between the two crosses. TRAP: Believing the gray cross moves when the white one passes through it; it remains anchored.

GOAL: Match the panel to two overlapping hub patterns using six precise clicks. CONTROLS: Click grid cells to cycle their colors; watch the side indicators for state changes. RULE: Each hub dictates a specific 3x3 region, with the shared middle row satisfying both constraints. TRAP: Assuming hubs are independent; the overlapping row is the key link that reduces total moves.

GOAL: Set the grid to a target pattern by flipping colors to match the logic of overlapping center zones. CONTROLS: Click a cell to toggle its color between red and orange. RULE: Each hub defines a zone where cell colors are determined by the hub's center color, creating consistent overlaps. TRAP: Assuming all cells cycle through more than two colors or that hubs themselves need to be clicked.

GOAL: Move three shapes to cover specific dots. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor; SPACE selects an object. RULE: Press SPACE until the cursor aligns with an object’s center to grab it. TRAP: Assuming the cursor stays fixed; it cycles, so you must press SPACE repeatedly to find the right object.

GOAL: Move two yellow tiles to specific target spots on the grid. CONTROLS: Red and green arrows shifted tiles along three separate tracks in opposite directions. RULE: Each arrow click shifted every tile on its track one step toward the arrowhead. TRAP: Assuming the outer border was a single loop; it was actually three independent tracks.

GOAL: Move the selected block into the ring’s interior. CONTROLS: Arrows slide the active block; clicking a block’s dot selects it. RULE: The block fits only when its lower rows align with the ring’s empty center. TRAP: Assuming any overlap counts; the block must be fully inside the ring’s hollow space.

GOAL: Guide the block to the target zone to trigger the win condition. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the block one grid step per press. RULE: The block snaps to fixed grid intervals, so plan movements in five-step jumps. TRAP: Believing the rotating dial or symbols must match the box to win; only final position matters.

GOAL: Paint specific grid cells orange to match a hidden target pattern. CONTROLS: Clicking a cell cycles its color through blue, red, then orange. RULE: Cells connected to orange hubs must become orange; blue hubs keep blue cells. TRAP: Assuming all cells in a region need the same color; only specific hub-linked cells change.

GOAL: Match shapes to dots by moving and recoloring them. CONTROLS: Arrows move shapes; Space cycles selection; O button fills areas to change shape color. RULE: Colors must match perfectly; a shape only counts if its color matches the dots it covers. TRAP: Assuming proximity alone clears dots; mismatched colors persist even when shapes cover the correct positions.

ESTABLISHED: Two identical blue blocks exist within a black maze region surrounded by colored cells. Movement is restricted to open black paths. FAILED: Placing both blocks in the top row did not clear the level. Swapping blocks to visually identical start positions was rejected. GOAL IS NOT: Simply occupying the top row. CONTROLS: Directional inputs move single blocks along open paths; merging into a two-cell bar is possible but constrained by colored walls.

GOAL: Place the yellow tile in the left bracket and the orange tile in the right bracket. CONTROLS: Left arrows rotate the left track; right arrows rotate the right track. RULE: Each click shifts tiles one step along the track, with the ends wrapping around. TRAP: Assuming the order of colors in the brackets doesn't matter leads to a wasted swap.

GOAL: Move two blocks until they occupied the same row with just one empty space between them, then pushed them toward each other to clear the level. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved both blocks simultaneously in the chosen direction, stopping if blocked by walls or each other. RULE: When blocks collided head-on, they merged, instantly solving the puzzle. TRAP: Trying to steer blocks independently wasted time; remember they always move as a single unit.

ESTROLISHED: The top-left HUD displays two ring icons (blue and gray) with a shrinking step bar. The gray block vanishes on contact without changing player color or the laser barrier. FAILED: Absorbing the gray block and pressing SPACE did not disable the laser or alter the HUD state. GOAL IS NOT: The red blob is not the primary objective; the blue ring remains the likely target despite current blockage. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player. SPACE interacts with objects but currently yields no visible effect on hazards or HUD.

GOAL: Guide yellow and orange tokens into their matching colored brackets on the bottom row. CONTROLS: Click arrows to slide entire rows left or right, or click side arrows to shift columns up or down. RULE: Tokens wrap around the grid edges, so moving right from the last column places you in the first column. TRAP: Assuming tokens stop at the board's edge wastes time; they cycle continuously, allowing long-range movement with few clicks.

GOAL: Move yellow tiles to the two brackets. CONTROLS: Red and green arrows rotated tile groups. RULE: Tiles moved along invisible paths, wrapping around edges. TRAP: Assuming arrows only affect nearby tiles, missing the long-distance loops.

GOAL: Fit four blocks into matching sockets. CONTROLS: Click block, use arrows to move. RULE: Blocks fill sockets only when shape and size match. TRAP: Assuming a block fits if it looks similar; exact alignment is required.

GOAL: Rotate the dial to match the box's orientation. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the player to step on targets. RULE: Stepping on a target rotates the dial; matching the box's glyph shape clears the level. TRAP: Assuming the box glyph was a new shape instead of a rotated version of the current dial state.

GOAL: Move the charcoal block onto the static yellow target zone. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move both black and charcoal blocks simultaneously in mirrored directions. RULE: Charcoal’s position must exactly match the yellow shape’s coordinates to win. TRAP: Assuming you could move blocks independently; they always shift together as a mirrored pair.

GOAL: Guide the green token to dock the yellow cross and square into their matching outlines. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the green token; pushing a yellow token shifts it one cell. RULE: A yellow token only locks into place when its shape perfectly fills the outline’s interior. TRAP: Assuming you can push a token while standing in the target outline; you must stand adjacent to push it in.

GOAL: Move the shape pair to cover the yellow target. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active object; Space swaps active status between the wall and the shape. RULE: Only the object with white dots responds to arrow keys. TRAP: Assuming arrows move the shape regardless of dot color wastes moves on a locked pair.

ESTABLISHED: The 2x2 ball moves freely through gray and colored zones. Rotating plugs alters walls but does not push the ball. FAILED: Moving right into the yellow pin area did not trigger a win. GOAL IS NOT: Simply landing on the yellow pin. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the ball two cells. Clicking plugs rotates their associated bars in place.

GOAL: Guide the ball to the yellow pin by navigating through shifting colored zones. CONTROLS: Arrows move the ball; clicking plugs rotates fixed blocks between horizontal and vertical positions. RULE: The ball passes through colored areas only if their shape matches the ball's current position; rotate blocks to clear the path. TRAP: Assuming rotated blocks stay clear; they may block your path again if you move into their new orientation without checking.

ESTABLISHED: The plug’s channel is horizontal, 3 tall, and 15 long. The socket pins are 3 tall and point left. The plug’s cavity is 3 wide and 9 tall. FAILED: Aligning the horizontal channel with vertical socket frames or pins for insertion. GOAL IS NOT: Inserting the plug body into the socket cavity or receiving the socket frame. CONTROLS: Rotation pivots the plug. Movement shifts the plug horizontally toward the socket pins.

ESTABLISHED: The BOTTOM pose pours a bottom band; the TOP pose pours a top band. FAILED: Painting the bottom band purple while the top band was already purple resulted in an all-purple canvas, not the split-color goal. GOAL IS NOT: A fully purple canvas or a fully white canvas. CONTROLS: LEFT/RIGHT rotate the pose; SPACE pours the selected color onto the canvas.

GOAL: Paint the bottom rows white while keeping the top purple. CONTROLS: Arrow keys rotate the paint bucket’s pouring direction; Space executes the pour. RULE: The bucket only pours in its current facing direction, so you must rotate it to point downward. TRAP: Assuming the rotation loops freely from bottom to top; it is a limited path, requiring specific upward steps to return.

ESTABLISHED: Water fills all connected spaces; the boat floats at the highest level. A dam exists below, but the room underneath is also full, preventing descent. A right-side passage is blocked by a wall the boat cannot reach directly. FAILED: Moving left into a cleared pocket did not allow the boat to bypass the central wall. Descending by draining water failed because the lower room is flooded. GOAL IS NOT: Draining the current room to lower the boat. CONTROLS: Clicking blocks removes them; arrow keys move the boat.

GOAL: Fill rows 0-4 purple, rows 5-9 white, and the bottom-right triangle orange. CONTROLS: Space pours the selected color; arrow keys move the stamp; clicks change the active color. RULE: Overlapping pours work if the final layer covers the rest, allowing two pours to fix four regions. TRAP: Assuming every distinct color zone needs its own separate pour step.

GOAL: Fit the T-shape into the left-side gap beneath the wall. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected object; Space cycles selection to the wall or shapes. RULE: Dots pass through solid walls, so lower the T before shifting it left. TRAP: Moving the T left first causes it to collide with the wall; always drop it below the barrier first.

GOAL: Insert the plug's prongs fully into the socket's pins to complete the circuit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the plug horizontally or vertically; the spacebar rotates the plug ninety degrees. RULE: The prongs must align precisely with the pin holes; side-by-side contact does not count as insertion. TRAP: Believing that visual alignment or touching the socket face was sufficient, causing wasted moves instead of rotating and pushing in.

GOAL: Guide the boat through the shaft to touch the pink target. CONTROLS: Arrows steer the boat; clicks clear obstacles. RULE: The boat only rises when moving horizontally into an open vertical space. TRAP: Moving left to align with the target traps the boat at the ceiling; stay aligned with the shaft to rise correctly.

GOAL: Position two shapes to perfectly cover the target outline. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selected piece; Space switches between pieces. RULE: Pieces can overlap each other and pass through walls to reach the goal. TRAP: Assuming walls block movement or that pieces cannot overlap during placement.

GOAL: Deliver two distinct tokens to their matching targets to clear the level. CONTROLS: Click grid cells to slide adjacent tokens one step toward the clicked location. RULE: A token is delivered only when its entire shape rests fully inside the matching colored zone. TRAP: Thinking you could drop the first token and finish; both specific tokens must reach their respective zones.

GOAL: Move two blocks into the same cell to merge them. CONTROLS: Arrow keys slide blocks until they hit a wall or another block. RULE: Blocks stop at obstacles, requiring careful positioning to align them for a collision. TRAP: Assuming blocks slide past each other; they actually stop, so plan paths to avoid blocking each other prematurely.

GOAL: Guide the ball to the pin while managing rotating obstacles. CONTROLS: Arrows move the ball; clicking blocks rotates them. RULE: Rotating a block changes the path, requiring precise timing. TRAP: Assuming rotations are instant or predictable without testing often leads to dead ends.

GOAL: Reach the exit while dodging enemies and navigating hidden floor tiles. CONTROLS: Arrow keys slide the player until hitting a wall or stop tile. RULE: Enemies move predictably, leaving white stop tiles where they vacate. TRAP: Assuming a cell is empty because an enemy is currently there, ignoring the underlying stop tile.

GOAL: Fill specific grid regions with four distinct colors using a movable stamp tool. CONTROLS: Arrows rotate the stamp’s orientation, clicks select paint colors, and space pours the paint. RULE: The stamp pours paint only into the grid cells aligned with its current open mouth. TRAP: Assuming the stamp moves across the grid; arrows only rotate it in place, requiring precise orientation alignment before pouring.

GOAL: Fill the board with distinct color zones: a blue left band, an orange top triangle, and purple elsewhere. CONTROLS: Arrows rotated the stamp to align with different board edges; clicks selected paint colors; space applied paint. RULE: Each stamp orientation painted a specific geometric region, allowing complex shapes to be built by combining simple directional pours. TRAP: Believing the stamp moved the paint source directly rather than rotating the applicator, causing misaligned pours.

GOAL: Fill four corners with specific colors while keeping the center block red. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor, clicks select colors or targets, and space pours paint. RULE: Paint order matters; later pours overwrite earlier ones, so apply broad regions before specific details. TRAP: Assuming the diagonal split is independent of the orange border caused wasted moves re-painting.

GOAL: Guide the ball to the purple-pin box to release a hidden button, then activate it to solidify obstacles for the final path. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the ball through corridors and boxes. Clicks activated the newly revealed purple button on the side panel. RULE: Entering a container with a pin releases that pin and spawns its corresponding button. TRAP: Assuming the button was ready from the start wasted time; you had to physically deliver the ball to the socket first.

GOAL: Align the piece with its mirror reflections by moving the grid walls. CONTROLS: Arrows shift the selected wall or piece; Space cycles the active element. RULE: The piece casts horizontal and vertical shadows across the walls; match them to the dark regions. TRAP: Moving the piece directly often fails; you must shift the walls to reposition the reflections first.

GOAL: Reposition the green socket and U-plug together so the U stays engaged while the green aligns with the yellow. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active piece; clicking selects a piece to activate it. RULE: Moving two engaged pieces by the same vector preserves their connection, allowing complex alignments. TRAP: Believing the U must move alone first; it disengages if not moved with the green simultaneously.

GOAL: Guide the player to the exit while navigating past moving enemies. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one space in the chosen direction. RULE: Enemies move two spaces per turn; if they meet head-on, they stop and reverse direction. TRAP: Assuming enemies pass through each other or continue moving after a collision wastes turns; remember they halt and flip.

GOAL: Deliver boxes to dock cells by coordinating moves with an NPC partner. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player and drag attached boxes; Space attaches or releases a box. RULE: The player must stand directly adjacent to the dock cell, with the box positioned between them and the target square. TRAP: Assuming the NPC targets the nearest box; they may ignore it, forcing you to switch targets mid-plan.

GOAL: Guide two agents to fill matching sockets while positioning a central cross correctly. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected agent or push obstacles; clicks select agents. RULE: Pushing an obstacle against a wall or another object stops movement immediately, preventing overshoot. TRAP: Believing a push moves the full distance; it stops early if blocked, requiring precise alignment.

GOAL: Align scattered blocks to form a solid yellow rectangle. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected piece; Space cycles selection among walls and shapes. RULE: Walls are non-blocking, allowing pieces to pass through them freely. TRAP: Assuming walls block movement wastes actions; they only serve as visual guides or movable obstacles.

GOAL: Place three yellow tiles into the top sockets. CONTROLS: Horizontal arrows rotate arms; vertical arrows shift rows; the center button swaps specific tiles. RULE: Rotations only cycle tiles within the main snowflake, keeping socket positions static until the final swap. TRAP: Assuming the extra tile on the upper arm rotates with the others; it stays fixed, requiring a specific swap to fill the gap.

ESTABLISHED: Clicking swaps the bar's identity with a target object. Arrow keys move the bar. Spills do not end the level. FAILED: Attempting to move objects without first swapping the bar to their identity. GOAL IS NOT: Simply placing objects anywhere; exact cell alignment is required. CONTROLS: Click to swap identities. Arrow keys move the current bar object.

GOAL: Move blocks to form three vertical channels. CONTROLS: Click to select, arrows to slide, space to pour. RULE: Liquid flows up through gaps and settles in cups below. TRAP: Placing blocks side-by-side blocks flow; stack them vertically instead.

GOAL: Align the yellow blocks with the target pattern by moving the vertical wall to the right and positioning the remaining pieces correctly. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selected object; Spacebar switches between objects; Enter confirms the solution. RULE: The wall moves independently of the pieces, requiring separate alignment steps for each component. TRAP: Assuming yellow blocks moved with the wall when they stayed fixed, causing unnecessary realignment attempts.

GOAL: Place one yellow in the row slot and the other in the grid slot. CONTROLS: N/S rotate the row and grid together; A/B shuffle the corner trio. RULE: The grid yellow needs a specific rotation count, while the row yellow needs a different phase. TRAP: Assuming N/S moves both yellows equally; you must use corner shuffles to hold one yellow back while rotating the other.

GOAL: Guide the green block from the bottom left into the top-right socket. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the block one step in the selected direction. RULE: Charcoal outlines are passable boundaries, not solid walls, allowing entry into the socket. TRAP: Assuming the outline blocks entry prevents the necessary downward move into the target area.

GOAL: Guide the ball along a horizontal bar to drop into a lower container and reach the yellow pin. CONTROLS: Click gray bars to make them passable; use arrow keys to move the ball. RULE: Only orange bars allow the ball to pass through; gray bars block movement. TRAP: Moving the ball before converting all necessary gray bars to orange causes the ball to fall or hit a wall, wasting moves.

GOAL: Merge all five boxes into the single dock area to complete the puzzle. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move your character to push or drag objects into place. RULE: Only one box can occupy a dock slot; extra boxes block the exit until rearranged. TRAP: Thinking the NPC moves independently; it actually mirrors your actions, so careless moves waste time.

GOAL: Arrange seven unique glyph shapes into a specific sequence to match the target row. CONTROLS: Arrow keys rotate the selected tile; spacebar confirms placement. RULE: Each of the seven rotation classes must appear exactly once in the solution. TRAP: Believing duplicate shapes belong to different classes; they are rotations of the same base form.

GOAL: Arrange blocks to form a zero-spill funnel for the liquid. CONTROLS: Click blocks to grab them, arrow keys to slide, space to pour. RULE: Only the block under your cursor moves; others stay fixed until grabbed. TRAP: Assuming you can move multiple blocks at once or that gravity helps align them.

GOAL: Match each blue slot’s glyph to the target letter’s shape class. CONTROLS: Left/Right moves the cursor; Up cycles the current glyph’s shape. RULE: Each slot requires a specific dihedral shape class; Up cycles through all seven classes. TRAP: Assuming E and B require different shapes; they share the same class, so one press fixes both.

ESTABLISHED: The puzzle requires routing a plug to a specific cell with a specific notch orientation. Columns process toggles sequentially, and the order of rotation versus movement within a column is currently unknown. FAILED: Attempts to solve the puzzle without first determining if rotations happen before or after movement bars within the same column. GOAL IS NOT: Simply placing the plug in the target cell; the plug’s notch must also face the correct direction. CONTROLS: Toggle switches to rotate the plug or move it up, down, left, or right. Launch the ball to execute the column’s instructi

GOAL: Transform seven pink glyphs into yellow targets by matching shape patterns. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor; UP cycles glyph rotation. RULE: Each input shape has exactly one matching output shape via rotation. TRAP: Assuming the grid starts at column 7; the first slot actually begins at column 8, causing off-by-one alignment errors.

ESTABLISHED: The pin sits at rows twenty-six to twenty-eight, columns forty-seven to forty-nine. The rotated zigzag’s tips must align eighteen columns apart across these positions. FAILED: Moving the original pin left twice without rotating the zigzag correctly left it stranded and misaligned. GOAL IS NOT: Simply sliding the pin to the edge; the zigzag body must fit without blocking the pin’s path. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move pieces horizontally. The space bar rotates the zigzag ninety degrees clockwise, shifting its orientation.

GOAL: Guide the block to the exit before the energy bar runs dry. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the block one step; passing over rings restores energy. RULE: The energy bar acts as a strict move counter, requiring precise pathing. TRAP: Assuming the warp tile only moves you vertically, rather than teleporting you across the board.

GOAL: Slide past patrolling enemies to reach the exit without touching active threats. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player; movement continues until hitting a wall or obstacle. RULE: Enemies patrol fixed paths; timing your slide to cross their path between cycles is key. TRAP: Assuming enemies stop instantly at edges; they may pause or reverse, requiring precise timing to avoid collision.
GOAL: Move beads to matching rings. CONTROLS: Click empty spaces to pull beads. RULE: Beads follow the longest unbroken path. TRAP: Assuming rods block movement; they do not.

GOAL: Deliver a peg to the room entrance. CONTROLS: Click the valve to move it; click a peg to jump it. RULE: A peg can jump over an adjacent obstacle to land on an empty spot. TRAP: Assuming the peg on the valve is stuck; it can actually jump into the room to complete the level.

ESTABLISHED: Two blocks exist. A cursor moves through corridors and can grab blocks. Clicking a corridor cell drops the cursor. FAILED: Moving blocks into adjacent cells did not clear the level. Clicking a block directly did not trigger a win. GOAL IS NOT: Simply placing two blocks in the same cell or adjacent cells. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the cursor or a held block. Clicking a block grabs it. Clicking a corridor drops it.

ESTABLISHED: The plug sits at row 28. Water levels are currently 46 and 64. Clicking the band area produces no change. The system remains stable at these values. FAILED: Clicking the band coordinates directly. Waiting for automatic transfer while the plug is aligned. Attempting to force transfer by adjusting water levels to match band boundaries. GOAL IS NOT: Aligning the plug with the band while maintaining current water heights. The solution does not require static alignment at these specific levels. CONTROLS: Clicking side buttons adjusts water volume. The band is currently inert to direct

GOAL: Guide the five-by-five block into the dark chamber to cover the hidden glyph. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the block one step at a time across the maze floor. RULE: The block can only pass through the glyph if the dial matches the pattern. TRAP: Thinking the black chamber walls were solid; they are actually walkable floor.

ESTABLISHED: Yellow key descends only to rows 42-44, blocked by Sky key cap. Sky key body obstructs path. FAILED: Pressing yellow key 4th time; extending yellow key right at rows 42-44 (blocked by leg). GOAL IS NOT: Placing yellow key at rows 45-47 via current Sky key configuration. CONTROLS: Pressing yellow key moves it down 3 rows until hitting Sky key cap or leg.
